entry.title: Uniform Intersection Numbers and Subgroup-Based Generating Graphs of Groups
entry.summary: The uniform intersection number of a finite group $G$, denoted by $ui(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the intersection of any $k$ distinct maximal subgroups of $G$ is equal to its Frattini subgroup. We determine the uniform intersection number of dicyclic, dihedral, and quasi-dihedral groups. We then investigate the uniform intersection number through the subgroup-based generating graph $\mathcal{G}(G)$ of a finite group $G$. We characterize the finite groups $G$ for which both the intersection number and the uniform intersection number are equal to two, and show that this condition is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}(G)$ being complete multipartite. We also classify finite groups in terms of the diameter, girth, and perfectness of $\mathcal{G}(G)$. Finally, we show that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $n=p_1^{r}p_2^{r}$, where $r\geq 2$ and $p_1$ and $p_2$ are distinct primes.

entry.title: Global transfer systems and endopurity of subgroups
entry.summary: Global transfer systems are combinatorial objects that parametrize intermediate levels of structures and properties in globally equivariant homotopy theory. In this paper we study the lattice of global transfer systems, expanding beyond the case of abelian groups which was computed by the second author. The main result is a proof that the irreducible elements of the lattice of global transfer systems are strictly controlled by subgroups of groups which we refer to as endopure. From the irreducible elements one can recover the whole lattice, and studying these endopure subgroups leads us to a wide range of new phenomena and computations.

entry.title: Locally indicable groups outside Brodskiĭ's quasivariety
entry.summary: We provide a set of group properties that together obstruct membership in the quasivariety that Brodskiĭ constructed in his proof that torsion-free one-relator groups are locally indicable. There are examples of locally indicable groups with these properties, which implies that Brodskiĭ's quasivariety is strictly contained in the quasivariety of all locally indicable groups. This disproves a conjecture of Howie.

entry.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
entry.summary: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.

entry.title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
entry.summary: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

entry.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
entry.summary: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.

entry.title: Only their cardinality can prevent groups from being quotients of weakly branch groups
entry.summary: It is a well-known fact that every proper quotient of a branch group is a virtually abelian group. We record that every group of cardinality at most $2^{\aleph_0}$ is a quotient of a weakly branch group; in fact, there are weakly branch groups that are split extensions with free complements. Furthermore, if a group is generated by $d$ elements, there is a weakly branch group generated by $(d+2)$ elements mapping onto it. As applications of this fact, we resolve a question of Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch but non-branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index and, partially, a question of Cox and Thillaisundaram on the existence of weakly branch groups that are not invariably generated.

entry.title: Automorphisms of triality groups over local rings
entry.summary: Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative local ring with $2,3\in R^\times$, and let $ρ\in\Aut(R)$ satisfy $ρ^3=\id$. We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full triality groups in the adjoint and simply connected forms of type $D_4$. Every automorphism is uniquely determined by an adjoint group element and a ring automorphism preserving the trace $T=\id+ρ+ρ^2$; conversely, every such pair defines an automorphism. A square-zero example shows that trace-preserving coefficient automorphisms need not normalize $\langleρ\rangle$ when $ρ$ is nontrivial on $R$ but trivial on its residue field. We also prove a relative rigidity theorem for homomorphisms from elementary triality groups over arbitrary coefficient rings to local targets with $2$ and $3$ invertible, assuming that an adjoint conjugation makes the parameter-one root images standard modulo the maximal ideal. Conversely, every unital trace-preserving ring homomorphism into such a local coefficient ring induces the corresponding homomorphism of elementary groups.

entry.title: Two-element factors and finite bases for additively idempotent semirings
entry.summary: For every additively idempotent semiring $S$ in the constant-free signature, $S$ is finitely based if and only if $S\times E$ is finitely based when $E=M_2$ or $T_2$. For each $E\in\{L_2,R_2,D_2,N_2\}$, both implications fail in general: we give a finitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is nonfinitely based and a nonfinitely based semiring whose product with $E$ is finitely based.

entry.title: A simultaneous variant of the Hall-Paige theorem and applications
entry.summary: For $k\geq 1$ , we say that a finite group $G$ satisfies property $\mathcal P_k$ if, for every $β_1,\ldots,β_k\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, there exists a bijection $f$ of $G$ such that each map $g\mapsto β_i(g)f(g)$ is a bijection. For $k=1$ this is equivalent to the classical Hall--Paige complete mapping property. We prove that if $p$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, then $G$ satisfies $\mathcal P_k$ for every $k<p-1$ and we show that this bound is sharp. For finite abelian $p$-groups, the bijection $f$ may moreover be chosen to be an automorphism, and for noncyclic homocyclic $p$-groups this remains true for $k=p-1$. Finally, we interpret $\mathcal P_k$ in terms of common transversals and common orthogonal mates of Latin squares generated from automorphisms and the Cayley table of a finite group $G$.

entry.title: Random Quotients of Hyperbolic Spaces with Respect to WPD Actions and Linear Connectivity of the Boundary
entry.summary: We study random quotients of acylindrically hyperbolic groups and hierchically hyperbolic groups, whose (partial) hyperbolicity is captured by their actions on Gromov hyperbolic spaces. We show that if an acylindrically hyperbolic group $G$ acts on a Gromov hyperbolic space $X$ coarsely transitively with a WPD element, then the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has linearly connected boundary. If $G$ is a group with a (relative) hierarchically hyperbolic group structure, with a quasi-tree top domain $X$, then in fact the quotient of $X$ by the normal closure of a random element of $G$ has boundary homeomorphic to the Nöbeling curve.

entry.title: Applications of $C^*$-Entropy to Representation Growth for Discrete Groups
entry.summary: The topological $1$-bounded entropy $h^\text{top}(C^*(Γ))$ of the full group $C^*$-algebra of a finitely generated group $Γ$ is given a representation-theoretic interpretation. The implications of Hilbert-Schmidt and matricial stability in this setting are investigated, recovering and strengthening a representation growth result of Hadwin and Shulman. The entropy framework is used to recover upper bounds on representation growth for superrigid groups and property (T) groups. This recovers a result of De La Harpe, Robinson, and Valette on the growth rate of the irreducible unitary representations of a property (T) group within the framework of $1$-bounded entropy. A soft proof that $SL_n(\mathbb{Z})$ admits subexponential representation growth is recorded.

entry.title: Automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over local rings
entry.summary: We classify abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2E_6$ over commutative local rings with involution and $2$ invertible, for both isogeny types. Every automorphism is standard, with no invertibility assumption on $3$. In the adjoint case, it has a unique expression as a composition of conjugation by an element of the full twisted group and a ring automorphism commuting with the involution. For the simply connected form, the full group equals its elementary subgroup, and the factors are strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms. The main step replaces a linear change of basis by a group element. Invariant alternating tensors determine the transported Chevalley bracket. We correct this bracket over a faithfully flat local extension and descend the resulting conjugating element by uniqueness. Root-subgroup relations then recover the coefficient automorphism.

entry.title: Quadratic fields of values of finite solvable groups
entry.summary: We show that if $G$ is a finite solvable group such that $E = \mathbb Q(\{χ(g)\, |\, χ\in{\rm Irr}(G),\ g \in G\})$ is an extension of degree 2 over the rationals, then $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{\pm d})$ for a positive integer $d$ all of whose prime divisors lie in $\{2, 3, 5\}$. Moreover, if $G$ has a composition factor of order 7, then either $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{2})$ or $E = \mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. This provides a partial answer to a question of G. Navarro.

entry.title: Resolutions of orbifold generalised triangle groups
entry.summary: Let $T=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}=1\rangle$ be a generalised triangle group in which $W$ is the Farey word of a rational slope $q=r/s$, and suppose that $T$ is the fundamental group of a hyperbolic $3$-orbifold whose singular locus has no spherical vertices. Let $G=\langle f,g\mid f^{l}=g^{m}=W^{n}\rangle$ be the associated central extension. We compute an explicit free resolution of the trivial module over $\mathbb{Z}G$ of minimal length, with differentials given in closed form by Fox derivatives. From this resolution we deduce an explicit free resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ which is $2$-periodic in degrees at least two, and we compute the integral homology and cohomology of both groups. Strebel treated the classical family $q=0/1$ in 1983. Since then only the family $q=1/2$ has been treated, by Ellis and Williams, and for that family our resolution over $\mathbb{Z}T$ has strictly smaller rank in every degree.

entry.title: Canonical Kummerian Kernels in 1-Smooth Pro-$p$ Poincaré Duality Groups of Dimension Three
entry.summary: Let $(G,θ)$ be a finitely generated 1-smooth oriented pro-$p$ group with torsion-free orientation, and suppose that $G$ is a Poincaré duality pro-$p$ group of dimension three. The orientation determines a canonical closed normal subgroup $K_θ(G)$ contained in the Frattini subgroup, and for a Kummerian pair the quotient $G/K_θ(G)$ is the maximal $θ$-abelian quotient. We prove that \[K_θ(G)\text{ finitely generated} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad K_θ(G)=1.\] Thus every non-$θ$-abelian 1-smooth $\textrm{PD}^3$ pro-$p$ group has an infinitely generated canonical kernel, where ``infinitely generated'' means not topologically finitely generated. The proof combines the normal-subgroup theorem for pro-$p$ $\textrm{PD}^3$ groups with the classification of $p$-adic analytic 1-smooth pro-$p$ groups. We also obtain a cohomological description of the canonical extension from the Hochschild--Serre five-term sequence and Poincaré duality. Writing $K=K_θ(G)$, $Q=G/K$, and $V=H^1(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, we identify $H^1(K,\mathbb{F}_p)^Q$ with the kernel of the map $\bigwedge^2V\to V^*$ induced by the triple cup-product form of $G$. Consequently, whenever $K\neq1$, its first cohomology is infinite-dimensional, whereas its $Q$-invariant subspace is nonzero and finite-dimensional. We obtain exact dimension restrictions in small generator ranks and show that a non-$θ$-abelian group with $2\leq d(G)\leq4$ is not Bloch--Kato. In the finitely generated-kernel case, $G$ is a three-dimensional uniform $θ$-abelian group with exterior mod-$p$ cohomology.

entry.title: Universally extendible characters
entry.summary: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_θ\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.

entry.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
entry.summary: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $Γ_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ Γ_n(M)/K_n(M)\congπ_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.

entry.title: Generation by lazy and invertible cellular automata over the Klein four-group
entry.summary: Let $G=C_2\times C_2$ and $A=\{0,1\}$. We characterize the submonoid of $\text{CA}(G;A)$ generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata. A cellular automaton belongs to this submonoid if and only if, whenever it maps the two free $G$-orbits onto the same free orbit, it maps both constant configurations and some two-point orbit to the same constant. The proof gives a factorization using elementary orbit collapses and three two-cell lazy maps. The criterion yields the cardinality $59\,712$ and identifies the maps missed by a weaker constant-separation invariant. Adjoining one idempotent generates the full monoid, and the generated submonoid is contained in exactly one maximal proper submonoid, of cardinality $65\,024$. The submonoid generated by lazy maps alone has $4\,007$ elements, and for both generating sets the maximum shortest-word length is six. The criterion and the cardinalities $59\,712$ and $4\,007$ are formally verified in Lean.

entry.title: Equational theories of flat semirings $S(W)$
entry.summary: We study the finite basis problem for flat semirings of the form $S(W)$, where $W$ is a nonempty set of nonempty words, possibly infinite. We prove that $S(W)$ is finitely based if and only if the strict interior of every word in $W$ is linear; here the strict interior of a word is obtained by deleting its first and last letters. This completely resolves an open problem raised by Jackson et al.~(J. Algebra 611: 211--245, 2022).

entry.title: The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings
entry.summary: For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.

entry.title: The finite basis problem and subvariety intervals for max-plus matrix semirings
entry.summary: Let $S=(\N,\max,+)$ be the max-plus algebra of the nonnegative integers, and let $\overline S$ be obtained from $S$ by adjoining $-\infty$ as a semiring zero. We first prove that the varieties generated by the full matrix semirings $\Mat_n(S)$ and by the upper triangular matrix semirings $\UT_n(\overline S)$ form strictly ascending chains. Every interval between distinct members of either chain has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and contains a chain and an antichain of that cardinality. The proof uses finite syntactic semirings associated with prime-cycle languages and an independent family of identities. We then construct finite commutative ai-semirings from languages of monomials closed under divisibility and prove their bounded-variable property by cancellation, explicit integer evaluations and independence in a free abelian group. A loop-block identity for upper triangular matrices and dimension-independent cubic-padding identities for full matrices show that every variety in each of the above intervals has infinite axiomatic rank. In fact, every variety between $\V(S)$ and the variety generated by all full matrix dimensions has infinite axiomatic rank. These varieties are therefore nonfinitely based, also relative to the ai-semiring axioms. Finally, for every fixed full matrix dimension, we prove equational equivalence over all six positive or nonnegative integer, rational and real coefficient domains. The original convex-ideal countermodels and their full-matrix transfer proof are recalled separately for comparison; they are not used in the algebraic proofs. Throughout, the signature consists of two binary operations and contains no constant symbols.

entry.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
entry.summary: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

entry.title: On the maximum relational complexity of affine groups
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $Ω$. The relational complexity $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is the least integer $r\geq 2$ such that the $G$-orbit of every finite tuple is determined by the $G$-orbits of its $r$-subtuples; there is currently only a small collection of groups $G$ for which $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is known precisely. In this paper we study the relational complexity of finite affine groups acting naturally on a $d$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that every such group has relational complexity at most $d+2$ when $q>2$ and at most $d+1$ when $q=2$; we produce a complete classification of the primitive such groups for which these bounds are attained.

entry.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type
entry.summary: We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite. A proper wide open subgroupoid is prime if it admits no proper intermediate wide open subgroupoid. We prove a trichotomy for prime subgroupoids: they are minimal, arise from a clopen bipartition, or have a unique nonempty proper closed invariant set, which is nowhere dense. For a prime subgroupoid, the normalizer of its topological full group is maximal in the ambient topological full group precisely when it maps onto the ambient abelianization. An analogous criterion holds in every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup. For a minimal prime subgroupoid, its topological full group is maximal precisely when it equals its normalizer and the inclusion induces a surjection on first groupoid homology. We also describe all fully amplified maximal subgroups, namely those closed under local agreement. For Thompson's group $V$, the stabilizer of every simple type system is maximal, extending results of Belk, Bleak, Quick and Skipper for finite type systems and certain classes of infinite ones. Finally, every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup has continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic maximal subgroups acting minimally on the unit space.

entry.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
entry.summary: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.

entry.title: Prefixes of Coxeter elements are Coxeter elements of the reflection subgroups they generate
entry.summary: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.

entry.title: Invariable Generation of Groups of Homeomorphisms
entry.summary: We provide a sufficient condition for a group of homeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff space to be non-invariably generated, generalizing previous results proved using the dynamics of a group's action. We exhibit new applications among Scott-Röver-Nekrashevych groups and among groups of tree automorphism of with (almost) locally prescribed actions.

entry.title: Conformal dimension and self-similar groups
entry.summary: We study the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of spaces with locally expanding self-covering maps and, more generally, limit spaces of contracting self-similar groups. We show that the conformal dimension is characterized by combinatorial moduli associated with the Schreier graphs of these groups. We compare these moduli with contraction coefficients of self-similar group actions and with algebras of functions on the limit spaces satisfying asymptotic $p$-energy conditions. We also give conditions on the group when the conformal dimension is equal to the infimum of visual metrics on the self-similarity complex.

entry.title: An analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible classes and radicality for finite irreducible Coxeter groups
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $M$ a $G$-module, and $F$ a field. A continuous group homomorphism $i : Γ_L=\text{Gal}(L_{\text{sep}}/L) \rightarrow G$ yields a homomorphism $i^* : H^d(G,M) \rightarrow H^d(L,M)$ for every $d\in \mathbb{N}$. An element $u \in H^d(G,M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $u\in\ker(i^*)$ for every $i$ and every field extension $L/F$. If $M=\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$ with a trivial $G$-action, an element $u$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if $u^k$ is negligible over $F$ for some $k\geq1$. The (eventually) negligible elements over $F$ form an ideal of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, called the (eventually) negligible ideal. We prove an analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible elements. An element $u\in H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if and only if the restriction of $u$ to the cohomology of each elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ is eventually negligible over $F$. Paired with applications of a Gysin-type long exact sequence, we identify generators of the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of dihedral groups, cyclic $2$-groups, and generalized quaternion groups. We prove that the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of every finite irreducible Coxeter group is radical. The result was previously known for Weyl groups; we prove it for the remaining non-Weyl types $I_2(m)$, $H_3$, and $H_4$.

entry.title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
entry.summary: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$. We discuss applications to several topics, including abelianizations of cyclically presented groups, homology groups of cyclic branched covers of knots, adjacency matrices and shifted graph Laplacians, $K$-theory, and Smith forms of matrix powers. For example, for two families of hyperbolic knots we give the first integral homology in every covering degree; or, when $g$ is squarefree, we determine the least eventual period of the Smith forms of powers of $f(C_g)$.

entry.title: The Euler Characteristic of Spherical Bestvina-Brady Kernels
entry.summary: We compute the Euler characteristic of Bestvina-Brady kernels $\operatorname{BB}(Γ)$ for all Artin groups of spherical type. Our method involves discrete Morse theory to describe the cellular structure of a classifying space for the Bestvina--Brady kernel, through the action of $\operatorname{BB}(Γ)$ on non-integer level sets of the universal cover of the Salvetti complex. We extend the method of computation of $χ(\operatorname{BB}(Γ))$ to Artin groups that satisfy the $K(π,1)$-conjecture and whose nerves are rationally acyclic, and we provide an example by realising the projective plane as the nerve of a Coxeter group.

entry.title: Constructions and automorphisms of quandles
entry.summary: We prove that if M is an abelian group and X = Alex(M, phi) is a Latin Alexander quandle with id - phi in Aut(M), then Aut(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect C_Aut(M)(phi), Inn(X) is isomorphic to M semidirect <phi> and Out(X) is isomorphic to C_Aut(M)(phi)/<phi>. As a consequence, we obtain a description of the automorphism groups of direct products of the cyclic commutative medial quandles C_{2n+1} and the dihedral quandles R_{2n+1}, and we find their orders. Furthermore, we correct a result of Bardakov-Fedoseev [Algebra and Logic 63 (2024), no. 2, 111-142] on multiplication of quandles and prove that the Borodin-Neshchadim-Simonov and Markhinina-Nasybullov quandles can be constructed from conjugation, core, and generalized Alexander quandles, using the operation of multiplication of quandles. Finally, we consider the quotients of a quandle Q, namely the medialization Q^med, the commutativization Q^com, and the trivialization Q^tr. We prove that the conjugation quandle Conj(G) is medial if and only if gamma_2(G) <= Z(G); we find bounds for |Conj(G)^med| and prove that Core(G)^com is isomorphic to Core(G/<<g^3>>). We describe commutative generalized Alexander quandles and, as a consequence, find the commutativization of the dihedral quandle: R_n^com is isomorphic to R_gcd(n,3).

entry.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

entry.title: Lie groups are countably representable
entry.summary: We prove that every Lie group can be realized by permutations of a countable set, answering a classical question of Ulam. The key deformation construction originated in an argument produced by OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra during extended mathematical discussions.

entry.title: The group generated by a graph's derangements
entry.summary: We introduce the leap group of a graph, the subgroup of the symmetric group on the vertex set generated by graph derangements. We summarize historical results on graph derangements, which we call hops, and prove additional existence and complexity results. The leap groups of various canonical graphs are computed, and their behavior under basic graph operations is analyzed. We offer partial results on which groups can appear as leap groups, and study hops and leaps for infinite and directed graphs.

entry.title: A note on the proof of nonamenability of F
entry.summary: The goal of this note is to provide a human written exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that Thompson's group F is nonamenable.

entry.title: Finite groups with conjugacy classes of size $2p^n$
entry.summary: We extend Burnside's $p^a$-Theorem on conjugacy classes of prime-power size by proving that no non-abelian finite simple group possesses a conjugacy class of size $2p^n$ for any prime $p$ and $n\geq 0$. Based on this, we partially extend a well-known result of L. Kazarin by showing that, given a finite group $G$, the subgroup generated by a conjugacy class $x^G$ of size $2p^n$ where $x$ has odd order, is a solvable normal subgroup of $G$. If instead the subgroup $\langle x^G \rangle$ generated by such a class $x^G$ is non-solvable (which forces $x$ to have even order), then $p= 5$ and $\langle x^G \rangle/S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_5$, where $S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ denotes the solvable radical of $\langle x^G \rangle$.

entry.title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension
entry.summary: We study learning an unknown element $g$ of a group acting with finite orbits on a countable set, from examples $(x,gx)$. After a sample on $A$, the consistent hypotheses are the restrictions of a coset of the pointwise stabilizer of $A$, and the sample forces exactly the labels of points this stabilizer fixes; for a Galois group, they form the field generated by the data. Through this correspondence, multiclass dimensions become group invariants: the DS and graph dimensions equal the height, the Littlestone dimension the longest irredundant sequence length, and the teaching dimension the minimal base size. Among deterministic learners, symmetry makes empirical risk minimization optimal: on nondegenerate classes every consistent learner, whatever its tie-breaking, attains the optimal realizable sample complexity up to constant factors, and every consistent online learner the optimal mistake bound. Agnostically, every ERM's sample complexity exceeds the known lower bound by at most the DS-to-Natarajan ratio, up to constants. For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.

entry.title: The one percent property for free groups
entry.summary: We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $δ>0$ such that for every probability measure $μ$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $μ$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $μ$-mass at least $δ$.

entry.title: Groups with the fixed-point property
entry.summary: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

entry.title: $\mathrm{CS}\mathfrak{X}$-groups and free constructions
entry.summary: Let $\X$ be a variety of groups. A group $G$ is $\CSX$ if its maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal. We prove that the amalgamated free product of two $\CSX$-groups with a malnormal amalgam and without any involutions is again $\CSX$. Using this, we describe conditions under which the HNN-extension of a $\CSX$-group is $\CSX$.

entry.title: Quandles with isomorphic representation categories
entry.summary: We give two types of examples where two non isomorphic finite quandles have isomorphic enveloping groups. This implies that two non-isomorphic finite quandles can share isomorphic representation categories (as additive and tensor categories simultaneously).

entry.title: Matrix Waring Problem-III
entry.summary: Let $n,k$ be positive integers and $q$ be a prime power. We prove that there exists a real constant $C_k$ depending only on $k$ such that if $ \# M_n(\mathbb{F}_q) > C_k$ then every element in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is a sum of two $k$th powers, proving Larsen's conjecture.

entry.title: Zero divisors in group algebras of torsion-free groups in odd characteristic
entry.summary: A recent preprint constructs a finitely presented torsion-free group $G$ with a finite two-dimensional classifying space such that $\mathbb F_2[G]$ contains nonzero zero divisors. We extend this to every odd prime $p$: there is a finitely presented torsion-free group $G_p$, again with a finite two-dimensional classifying space, such that $\mathbb F_p[G_p]$ contains nonzero elements $α,β$ with $αβ=0$. Together with the case $p=2$, Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture therefore fails over every field of positive characteristic. The new ingredients are a signed version of the parity cancellation, made possible by a bipartite random model on one side; a type design built from the projective plane over $\mathbb F_{p^3}$ with $p$ additional letters, which makes every cross-intersection congruent to $1$ modulo $p$; and a squared-word decay estimate for this design, proved with an explicit test vector. The geometric part of the argument is taken from the characteristic-two construction. The characteristic-zero case remains open.

entry.title: Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow $2$-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups
entry.summary: A complete mapping of a finite group $G$ is a permutation $θ$ of $G$ such that $x\mapsto xθ(x)$ is also a permutation of $G$. Complete mappings have applications in cryptography, particularly in the design of round functions for cryptographic systems. The study of their parity has led to the question of which finite groups admit complete mappings of both parities. A useful approach to this question is to construct complete mappings stabilizing suitable subgroups, in particular Sylow $2$-subgroups. We show that, for every $n\geq2$, every prime power $q$, and every $Z\leq Z(\mathrm{SL}_n(q))$, the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(q)/Z$ admits a complete mapping stabilizing a Sylow $2$-subgroup if and only if $(n,q)\neq(2,2)$.

entry.title: On a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup
entry.summary: We provide a complete characterization of a finite group in which every non-supersolvable maximal subgroup is a TI-subgroup, which generalizes some known related results.

entry.title: A characterization of central extensions relative to n-nilpotent objects
entry.summary: We characterize the central extensions, in the sense of the categorical theory of central extensions of Janelidze and Kelly, relative to the Birkhoff subcategory of $n$-nilpotent objects of a semi-abelian and algebraically coherent category. An extension $f \colon A \to B$ with kernel $K$ turns out to be central precisely when the iterated Huq commutator $[A,[A,\dots,[A,K]\dots]]$, with $n$ occurrences of $A$, vanishes. For $n=2$ this condition reads $[A,[K,A]] = 0$, that is, $[K,A]$ is a central subobject of $A$. In the special case of groups this description was obtained by Everaert and the first author. The present proof is categorical, and applies in particular to Lie algebras, to crossed modules, to cocommutative Hopf algebras over a field, and to any category of interest.

entry.title: Classifying quasi-representations of groups via their characters
entry.summary: For every countable discrete group, we construct a character for finite-dimensional unitary quasi-representations, with values in the inverse limit of the equivariant $K$-theory of its Rips complexes. The character is a complete invariant for quasi-representations up to stable equivalence for amenable groups and, more generally, for groups satisfying the Haagerup property and QR-quasidiagonality. For Haagerup groups satisfying quantitative QR-quasidiagonality, we also obtain a quantiative version of the theorems. These conclusions apply when the maximal group $C^*$-algebra is quasidiagonal and has the lifting property, including amenable groups, free groups, and closed orientable surface groups. For surface groups, rank and winding number give complete invariants for the classification. Finally, composing with the equivariant Chern character gives a delocalized cohomological obstruction to stable equivalence of a quasi-representation with genuine representations.

entry.title: An explicit construction of a limit variety of groups
entry.summary: We construct an explicit countable group \(G_*=N(R)\rtimes A\) whose generated variety is a limit variety of groups: it has no finite identity basis, whereas every proper subvariety is finitely based. Here \(A\) is relatively free in the variety of groups of nilpotency class at most two and exponent dividing four, and \(R\) is an explicitly defined quotient of the group algebra \(\mathbb F_2[A]\). The proof establishes an ascending chain condition for coefficient spaces indexed by six ordered commutator entries and reduces every proper subvariety to a hereditarily finitely based approximation. Non-finite basability is obtained by transferring independent identities from the constructions of Gupta and Krasilnikov. The resulting variety is contained in \(\mathfrak B_4\mathfrak B_2\). This construction provides the first example of such a variety in which both the generators and a basis are explicitly given.

entry.title: Profinite recognition of uniformity
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a semisimple Lie group that is not isogenous to the isometry group of real or complex hyperbolic $n$-space. We show that the rational rank is a profinite invariant for irreducible lattices in $G$, unless $G$ has type $D_{2n}$ which forms a genuine exception. In particular, profinitely isomorphic lattices in $G$ of type $D_{2n}$ can have differing virtual cohomological dimension. As another corollary, uniformity is a profinite property for irreducible lattices in $G$ outside type $D_4$. Assuming CSP, the existence of triality symmetries gives uniform and non-uniform profinitely isomorphic lattices in type $D_4$.

entry.title: On a Combinatorial Characterization of Abelian Group Actions
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$ and $X$ a finite $G$-set. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on $G$ for any $X$ to be determined up to isomorphism by certain combinatorial data. Specifically, if $M_H^X$ is the number of $H$-orbits in $X$, and $a_d^X$ is the number of $G$-orbits in $X$ of cardinality $d$, we characterize when equalities $M_H^{X_1} = M_H^{X_2}$ and $a_d^{X_1}=a_d^{X_2}$ for all $H \leq G$ and $d|n$, respectively, force an isomorphism $X_1 \simeq X_2$. Our main result is that this occurs if and only if $G$ is cyclic or $G$ is the direct sum of a finite cyclic group and a cyclic group of prime order. We conclude with an arithmetic application to $L$-function factorization.

entry.title: Entropy, isoperimetry and the total variation profile of random walks
entry.summary: The total variation profile $\mathrm{TV}_n$ of a random walk measures how far its distribution at time $n$ is from being invariant under the generators. Three lower bounds are given: an elementary bound $\mathrm{TV}_n \geq 1/\big(44\,L(n)\big)$ in terms of the speed $L(n)$; a bound by the entropy increment $H(P^{n+1}) - H(P^n)$, which is a reverse Pinsker inequality; and a bound in terms of the entropy and the isoperimetric profile. Deciding whether the entropy-increment bound always improves on the isoperimetric one is related to conjectures on the growth of the entropy and of groups. The motivation comes from the question of whether the distributions of a random walk can be transported back onto their translates at bounded cost.

entry.title: On the local Frattini subgroup of a finite group
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $π(G)$ be the set of prime divisors of $|G|$. For each $p\in π(G)$, choose a Sylow $p$-subgroup $G_p$ of $G$. The subgroup $Ψ(G)= \prod_{p\in π(G)} Φ(G_p)_G$ is called the \textit{local Frattini subgroup} of $G$. Here, for $J \leqslant G$, the symbol $J_G$ denotes the core of $J$ in $G$. The subgroup $Ψ(G)$ is a characteristic subgroup of $G$ that is contained in $Φ(G)$, the Frattini subgroup of $G$. We prove that $Ψ(G)$ satisfies many properties similar to $Φ(G)$. Let $J$ be a normal $p$-subgroup of $G$ with $J \leqslant Φ(G)$, and let $S$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. John S. Rose proved that if $J \leqslant \mathbf{Z}(S)$, then $J \leqslant Φ(S)$. So, in fact, $J \leqslant Φ(S)_G \leqslant Ψ(G)$. Kaplan, Lev, Mann, and Solomon found various other conditions that would ensure $J$ is contained in $Φ(S)$. In this article, we add a few more conditions to this list.

entry.title: Multivalued Groups and Schur Rings
entry.summary: We study finite involutive multivalued groups associated with Schur rings. Their reduced valency is shown to equal the least common multiple of the sizes of the basic sets of the corresponding ring. We prove that the double-coset group associated with a complemented subgroup of a finite group is isomorphic to a Schur multivalued group over the complement. In particular, every coset multivalued group is a Schur multivalued group. Using affine Schur rings, we construct families of pairwise nonisomorphic commutative multivalued groups over elementary abelian groups. We obtain asymptotic bounds for the sizes of these families and prove that the proportion of double-coset groups in them tends to zero.

entry.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
entry.summary: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = τ+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $τ= -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.

entry.title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
entry.summary: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.

entry.title: A non-nilpotent localization of a finite p-group
entry.summary: We give negative answers to two questions of Farjoun about localizations of groups. For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite $p$-group $G$, an infinite non-nilpotent group $H$, and a local embedding $f\colon G\hookrightarrow H$. The associated localization satisfies $L_f(G)\cong H$, showing that localizations need not preserve nilpotence and that the localization map $G\to L(G)$ need not be surjective when $G$ is a finite $p$-group.

entry.title: The theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of groups
entry.summary: Motivated by recent work on $λ$-fold near-factorizations by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations as combinatorial structures with prescribed representation multiplicities. Such a factorization consists of two subsets of a finite group whose products represent each nonidentity element exactly $λ$ times and the identity exactly $μ$ times. These structures generalize $λ$-fold near-factorizations and provide a common framework for several families arising in combinatorial design theory, including strong external difference families with two equal-sized subsets, as well as binary sequence pairs with two-level correlation. Their associated $\{0,1\}$-matrices satisfy the Bridges-Ryser equation $XY=λ(J-I)+μI$, linking the factorization problem to a classical matrix framework for combinatorial designs. We establish the foundational theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.

entry.title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
entry.summary: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $μ_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.

entry.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
entry.summary: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

entry.title: Answer some Tkachenko's questions in factorizable semitopological groups
entry.summary: We construct a Hausdorff quasitopological abelian group that is second-countable and semiregular, with a bounded continuous function that does not factor through any regular first-countable semitopological group. Its regular and Tychonoff reflections coincide, have a countable network, and fail even factorizability through arbitrary first-countable semitopological groups. This gives negative answers to \cite[Problems~6.1, 6.2, 6.4, and~6.5]{Tk2026} of Tkachenko. The construction starts with a countable cone group whose common separation reflection is not Fréchet--Urysohn, answering \cite[Problems~6.8 and~6.9]{Tk2026} negatively. In contrast, symmetrization gives affirmative answers to \cite[Problems~6.6 and~6.7]{Tk2026} without separation assumptions. We also show that every countable semitopological group admits simultaneous factorizations of countable families through second-countable Tychonoff semitopological groups.

entry.title: Regular automorphisms of periodic $p'$-groups need not be splitting
entry.summary: For a fixed prime $p$, a group is called a $p'$-group if the orders of all its elements are coprime to $p$. It is well known that in a finite $p'$-group an automorphism of order $p$ is regular if and only if it is a splitting automorphism of period $p$. In the Kourovka Notebook, V.\,D.~Mazurov asked whether these two notions coincide for periodic $p'$-groups. We answer this question in the negative by constructing a periodic group of prime period $q$ that admits a regular automorphism of order $p \neq q$ which is not splitting.

entry.title: Three-point orbits of 2-transitive groups and their combinatorial applications
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a finite $2$-transitive permutation group. We determine the orbits of $G$ on the unordered triples of its point set, together with the three-point stabilizer and its image inside $S_3$, for every affine and almost simple family in the finite $2$-transitive classification. These data classify the $G$-invariant triple systems and the simple $2$-\mbox{$(v,3,λ)$} designs admitting $G$, and yield in a uniform way the standard objects attached to them: the incidence and block graphs (with arc-transitivity and strong regularity in the Steiner case), the constant-weight and design codes, and the Schurian coherent configurations on triples.

entry.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
entry.summary: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.

entry.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
entry.summary: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.

entry.title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
entry.summary: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.

entry.title: Sylow $2$-Subgroups of Finite Groups with a Single Conjugacy Class of Involutions
entry.summary: We solve Brauer's Problem 33 by determining the finite $2$-groups that occur as Sylow $2$-subgroups of finite groups with a single conjugacy class of involutions. Besides the Sylow $2$-subgroups arising from the relevant non-abelian simple groups in Table 1, these are precisely the homocyclic, generalized quaternion, and Suzuki $2$-groups. The classification of finite simple groups is used in this paper.

entry.title: Twisted Equations and Palindrome Length
entry.summary: Twisted equations in free groups are equations in which a finite group of symmetries acts on the free group by automorphisms and anti-automorphisms, such as inversion and reversal; moreover, the variables may be subject to rational constraints. Algorithms from the theory of equations in virtually free groups solve such equations in PSPACE, but they are intricate. Our main result is an elementary algorithm for quadratic twisted equations, which extends the algorithm of Comerford and Edmunds (1981) for quadratic equations in free groups to the twisted setting and to rational constraints. Besides deciding solvability in PSPACE and yielding EDT0L descriptions of solution sets, our algorithm computes, for every quadratic expression, finitely many parametric forms describing its values as freely reduced words. As an application, we study the palindrome length of elements of free groups, that is, the least number of palindromes whose product they are. Guided by the parametric forms that our algorithm computes for products of palindromes, we found, and then proved directly, a characterization of the freely reduced words of palindrome length at most $n$ in terms of patterns describing how palindromes are nested by twisted conjugations, thereby confirming a Catalan structure conjectured by the second author. Consequently, these words form a context-free language, and palindrome length is computable in cubic time as well as in LOGCFL, answering a question of Bardakov, Shpilrain, and Tolstykh (2005).

entry.title: Almost tight asymptotic enumeration of finite $p$-groups: Almost all finite groups are $2$-groups of class $2$
entry.summary: Let $f(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of groups of order $n$. We prove, uniformly over all primes $p$, that \[ \log_p f(p^m)=\frac{2}{27}m^3-\frac49m^2+O(m), \] with an absolute implied constant. This improves the classical upper bounds of Sims (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1965) and Newman--Seeley and matches Higman's lower bound (\emph{Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.}, 1960) through the quadratic term. We also prove that \emph{the proportion of $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$ among all groups of order at most $n$, counted up to isomorphism, tends to $1$ as $n\to\infty$.} These results answer questions~22.3 and~22.19 of Blackburn--Neumann--Venkataraman (\emph{Enumeration of Finite Groups}, 2007). Our proof refines Sims' enumeration framework using graded Lie brackets, constraints on deeper commutator coordinates, and incidence and Fourier estimates for alternating forms. Normalization by changes of generating bases then determines the quadratic term in the upper bound. We also prove that all but a $p^{-Ω(m^2)}$ fraction of groups of order $p^m$ have a central elementary abelian Frattini subgroup. Combining this concentration with the sharp enumeration bound of Bläser--Li--Qiao--Rogovskyy (\emph{arXiv}, 2025) for $p$-groups of Frattini class $2$ yields the linear error term. The same presentation estimates give fixed-quotient extension bounds which, together with Pyber's prescribed-Sylow theorem and the concentration result, establish domination by $2$-groups of nilpotency class $2$.

entry.title: Transposition Cayley Spectra and Subgraph Counts
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on the vertex set $[n]$, and let $Γ(G)$ be the Cayley graph of the symmetric group $S_n$ generated by the transpositions corresponding to the edges of $G$. We study the inverse spectral problem for the assignment $G\mapsto Γ(G)$ through the group-algebra operator $A_G=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(G)}(ij)$ and its regular spectral moments $M_k(G)=\operatorname{tr}(A_G^k)$. The moments admit two all-order forms: a universal support expansion in non-induced subgraph counts of $G$, and a representation-theoretic expansion over the irreducible representations of $S_n$. We compute the first nontrivial moments through order six. In particular, the fourth moment already contains the Coxeter triangle relation and determines the signed local invariant $6N_{K_3}(G)-N_{P_3}(G)$, rather than $N_{P_3}(G)$ alone. Consequently, for triangle-free graphs the spectrum determines the second moment of the degree sequence. We also give a simplified sixth-moment formula for triangle-free graphs, showing that in this class the spectrum determines $5N_{K_{1,3}}(G)+2N_{P_4}(G)+12N_{C_4}(G)$. Further structural consequences include bipartiteness and spectral symmetry of $Γ(G)$, a precise connectedness test, and the identification of the standard irreducible component with the shifted graph Laplacian $mI-L_G$.

entry.title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
entry.summary: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/γ_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.

entry.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Artin and Coxeter groups whose outer automorphisms are length-preserving
entry.summary: We prove that every length-preserving automorphism of a nonspherical Artin or Coxeter group has infinite Reidemeister number. As a consequence, we establish property $R_\infty$ for large-type free-of-infinity Artin groups, infinite strongly rigid Coxeter groups, and infinite virtually abelian Coxeter groups, including all affine Coxeter groups. We also prove that the automorphism group of every infinite irreducible non-affine strongly rigid Coxeter group is acylindrically hyperbolic.

entry.title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
entry.summary: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.

entry.title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
entry.summary: We complete the proof that every compact 3-manifold group is linear. Specifically, we construct a faithful representation in GL5(Q[u]) for a finite-index subgroup of every closed non-geometric graph-manifold group.

entry.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
entry.summary: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations. Likewise, since any action gives rise to a $C^*$-correspondence between the full cross-sectional $C^*$-algebras of the involved Fell bundles, we examine the connection between the $C^*$-correspondence associated with the tensor product of two given actions and the tensor product of the associated $C^*$-correspondences. We also discuss how the tensor product of actions naturally appears in Rieffel-like induction processes. Finally we present related results on the Fourier-Stieltjes and Fourier algebras of a Fell bundle.

entry.title: $D^L$, $D^Q$ Spectrum and Eigenvalue-free Interval of Cayley Graphs over Finite Nilpotent Groups
entry.summary: For a finite group $G$ and a symmetric connection set $S$, we study the distance Laplacian ($D^L$) and distance signless Laplacian ($D^Q$) spectrum of the Cayley graph $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ a finite nilpotent group. Using the internal direct product decomposition over Sylow subgroups, we reduce every question to a single (possibly non-abelian) prime-power factor. In this setting, the required tools are furnished by ordinary representation theory rather than character theory. Based on this framework, we then derive a complete and explicit formula for every eigenvalue, with multiplicity, of the distance matrix, distance Laplacian, and distance signless Laplacian of $\Cay(G,S)$ for $G$ nilpotent: each eigenvalue is indexed by a tuple of irreducible characters of the Sylow factors. Finally, we use the explicit spectrum, together with Perron--Frobenius theory, to determine the eigenvalue-free interval of $D^L$ and $D^Q$.

entry.title: On $p$-groups with one nonlinear codegree
entry.summary: For an irreducible character $χ$ of a finite group $G$, its codegree is defined by $cod(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$. In this paper, we characterize fnite $p$-groups whose nonlinear irreducible characters all have the same codegree.

entry.title: Recognizing oriented knots from finite quotients with one marked element
entry.summary: For an oriented tame knot $K$, let $G_K$ be its group, with positive meridian $μ_K$ and preferred longitude $λ_K$. We prove that the profinite completion $\widehat{G_K}$, marked by the conjugacy class of $μ_Kλ_K$, determines $K$ up to oriented equivalence. In fact, every isomorphism preserving this mark preserves the meridian and longitude with the same conjugator. The proof combines Xu's genuineness theorem with profinite JSJ theory and simultaneous boundary realization, and applies to satellite and composite knots. Consequently, Eisermann's colouring polynomials over all finite groups determine oriented knots.

entry.title: Classes of Subgroups of a finite group with isomorphic quotient groups
entry.summary: In this paper, we study the poset QIso(G) of classes of subgroups of a finite group G having isomorphic quotients. Particularly, we study it for finite abelian groups and for some classes of non-abelian metacyclic groups, namely dihedral groups Dn, the group U2np and affine groups Aff(F) over finite field F. In the case of abelian groups G, we show that there exists a duality from QIso(G) to Iso(G). We show that cyclic groups are the only groups for which QIso(G), up to duality is isomorphic to its subgroup lattice. We also show that cyclic groups are the only nilpotent groups for which QIso(G), up to duality is isomorphic to its lattice of normal subgroups. We characterize finite 2-groups all of whose subgroups are q-self dual with QIso(G) being a chain. We also characterize all p-groups G of order at most p4 whose QIso(G) is a chain.

entry.title: Cohomology and multiplicative gaps for quasi-isometries of nilpotent groups
entry.summary: We construct two word metrics on the same seven-dimensional torsion-free nilpotent lattice whose asymptotic cones are isometric, but for which every quasi-isometry has multiplicative constant at least $1+\varepsilon$, for one fixed $\varepsilon>0$. We use a convex invariant of a fixed quasi-isometry $Ψ:N\to M$. The displacement cocycle of $Ψ$ and the right-invariant means on $N$ determine a compact convex set $\mathcal A(Ψ)\subseteq\operatorname{Hom}(V_N,V_M)$. If $\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ)$ denotes the first-layer maps of the graded homomorphisms that occur as blow-downs of $Ψ$ with varying basepoints, then $$ \mathcal A(Ψ)=\operatorname{conv}\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ), \qquad\operatorname{Ext}\mathcal A(Ψ)\subseteq\mathscr G_{\mathrm{pt}}(Ψ). $$ For every extreme point $L\in\mathcal A(Ψ)$, the dual map $L^*$ is also the degree-one part of an isomorphism of the full real cohomology rings. This cohomological compatibility, together with the realization of first-layer Pansu differentials by invariant means, yields the multiplicative constant gap stated above.
entry.arxiv:comment: 34 pages. This is split off from the authors' previous submission arXiv:2512.06753. Comments are most welcome!

entry.title: On the number of conjugacy classes of finite solvable groups of order divisible by $p^2$
entry.summary: In 2003, Héthelyi and Külshammer proved that if $G$ is a finite solvable group and $p$ is a prime such that $p^2$ divides $|G|$, then $k(G)\geq (49p+1)/60$, and they constructed an infinite family of groups for which this bound was claimed to be attained. We point out that the groups in this family are not Frobenius groups, so that their class numbers are considerably larger than stated, and that in fact the bound is never attained. We then determine the best possible bound of this shape: we show that $k(G)\geq (49p+7)/60$ for all primes $p$, which is sharp for $p=17$, and that $k(G)\geq (49p+451)/60$ for all primes $p>2719$, which is sharp for infinitely many primes $p$. Thus the slope $49/60$ found by Héthelyi and Külshammer is best possible, but the correct additive constant is $451/60$ rather than $1/60$.

entry.title: Quasipositive Braids, Presentations, and Garside Structures
entry.summary: We provide a presentation of the braid group in which the generating set is the set of all positive half-twists, the relations are balanced positive relations, and every relation is conjugate to one in a finite list. We then prove that for any such presentation, its positive monoid is not isomorphic to the quasipositive braid monoid. Finally, we show that the quasipositive braid monoid has no proper Garside family. These results settle a problem of Calegari from the K3 problems list.

entry.title: LInearity of Tubular Groups
entry.summary: We prove that a tubular group is linear if and only if it is residually finite, equivalently virtually primitive. Every such group embeds in $\SL_n(\Z[u])$. For a primitive tubular decomposition with at most $m$ edge slopes at each vertex, our representation has dimension $2\max\{2,m\}$. In particular, Gersten's group embeds in $\SL_6(\Z[u])$, and this dimension is minimal.

entry.title: Minor exclusion and planar rigidity
entry.summary: We prove that every connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph which is quasi-isometric to a graph excluding a countable clique as a minor is quasi-isometric to a planar graph. Consequently, every finitely generated group with such a quasi-isometry is virtually planar, meaning that some finite-index subgroup admits a planar Cayley graph. We also show that a connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive graph admitting a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding some finite minor admits a regular map into a bounded-degree planar graph. If the source is accessible, the target need only exclude a countable clique. Combined with work of Mackay, Spriano, and the present author, this shows that a finitely presented group admits a regular map into a bounded-degree graph excluding a countable clique if and only if it is virtually planar.

entry.title: Coloring graphs of homologous spheres
entry.summary: The curve graph of a surface is the graph whose vertices are isotopy classes of essential, closed curves on the surface. Edges join vertices with disjoint representatives. The curve graph plays a central role in the theory of mapping class groups of surfaces. Gaster, Greene, and Vlamis have shown that the subgraph of the curve graph induced by curves in a single primitive homology class is uniquely and finitely colorable. In the analogy between the theory of mapping class groups of surfaces and outer automorphisms of free groups, the sphere graph of $M_r$, a connect sum of $r$ copies of $S_1 \times S_2$ plays an analogous role in the theory. Motivated by Gaster, Green, and Vlamis' result, we investigate $\mathcal{S}_v(M_r)$, the subgraph of the sphere graph of $M_r$ induced by spheres representing a single primitive homology class $[v] \in H_2(M_r;\mathbb{Z})$. We show that this graph is uniquely $r-1$ colorable. As a corollary, with $r\ge 3$ we obtain a nontrivial homomorphism from the Torelli subgroup $IO_r \le \operatorname{Out}(F_r)$ to the symmetric group on $r-1$ symbols; this parallels Gaster, Greene, and Vlamis' connection between their coloring and the Chillingworth homomorphism. In the course of our proof we find new smaller generating sets for mapping class groups of $M_r$ with spheres deleted.

entry.title: Ordinary $G$-permutable subgroups of finite simple groups
entry.summary: We completely solve part (a) of Problem 17.112 in the Kourovka Notebook. We prove that a non-abelian finite simple group $G$ has a proper non-trivial ordinary $G$-permutable subgroup if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to ${\rm PSL_2(q)}$ where $q\geq4$ is a prime power and $q\not\equiv3\pmod4$, ${}^2B_2(2^{2a+1})$ where $a\geq1$, $J_1$, ${\rm Sp}_4(4)$, or ${\rm PSp}_4(p)$ where $p$ is prime and $p\equiv1,13,17\pmod{24}$. Moreover, we classify all proper non-trivial ordinary $G$-permutable subgroups of these groups. Every other non-abelian finite simple group $G$ has no proper non-trivial ordinary $G$-permutable subgroup.
entry.arxiv:comment: This completely solves Problem 17.112(a) of the Kourovka Notebook

entry.title: A proof of the Galt--Tyutyanov conjecture on Skiba's question
entry.summary: A subgroup $A$ of a finite group $G$ is \emph{hereditarily $G$-permutable} if, for every subgroup $E$ with $A\leq E\leq G$ and every subgroup $B$ of $E$, some $G$-conjugate of $B$ permutes with $A$ in $E$. We give a new criterion for a finite group to be simple. A nontrivial finite group $G$ is simple if and only if it has no proper nontrivial hereditarily $G$-permutable subgroup. This proves the conjecture of Galt and Tyutyanov and answers Skiba's question in part \textup{(b)} of Problem 17.112 in the Kourovka Notebook. Earlier work settled the conjecture for alternating groups, sporadic groups, exceptional groups of Lie type, and the groups ${\rm PSL}_2(q)$ and ${\rm PSU}_3(q)$. We prove the conjecture for all classical groups. The proof uses descent through parabolic subgroups and the classification of factorizations of finite simple groups.
